case_schema.normalization: Normalize only explicitly enumerated temporary paths or volatile timestamps. Never normalize source revision, source digest, model/artifact identity, model revision, or SHA-256 values.
case_schema.fixture_policy: One small observed fixture may cover a positive/negative behavior boundary; grouped source references in behavioral_ownership are the remaining handoff. A Rust replacement must run the group's invariant, not copy a method name or source text assertion.
case_schema.status_note: Source test methods are references, not 1,764 required golden files. behavioral_ownership below groups concrete invariants; critical direct CLI observations are in fixtures. A later owner must execute equivalent positive/negative Rust or CTest behavior and relevant live/platform gates before deleting legacy assertions.

behavioral_ownership.contract: Each group lists source tests that assert an actual invariant, its future owner and required execution gate. Module rows retain the complete source method roster for reconciliation; group examples do not imply every source assertion was executed in Rust. A group can cover multiple parameterized inputs when they test the same decision. Source-only workflow assertions need workflow-contract checks plus live lane evidence, not renamed source-string tests.
